ops.issue: Wrong reading of 温く in context: beer losing its chill is ぬるい (lukewarm/tepid), read ぬるく. ぬくい 'nice and warm' is a regional/dialectal word and does not fit beer going warm; the gloss itself says 'lukewarm (losing its coolness)'.

ops.current: bi-ruganukukunatteshimatta
ops.fix: bi-ruganurukunatteshimatta
ops.issue: Same wrong reading carried into romaji: 温く should be romanized nuruku (from ぬるい 'lukewarm'), not nukuku.

ops.current: ぬくく
ops.fix: ぬるく
ops.issue: Token reading for 温く should be ぬるく (from ぬるい 'lukewarm', the standard word for drinks that lost their chill), not ぬくく (dialectal ぬくい 'nice and warm').

ops.current: As for the ashtray, it's already full.
ops.fix: The ashtray (が) is already full.
ops.issue: Literal mirror uses the topic device 'As for...' (the corpus's rendering of は) for the が-marked subject 灰皿が; the expl itself says が marks the subject, so the mirror conflates は and が for learners.

ops.current: Quanto ao cinzeiro, (ele) já (está) cheio.
ops.fix: O cinzeiro (が) já (está) cheio.
ops.issue: 'Quanto a...' is the corpus's は device, but 灰皿 is marked by が (subject). The literal mirror should show the subject relation, not a topic construction.

ops.current: As for the television, I put it on top of the stand.
ops.fix: The television, (I) put (it) on top of the stand.
ops.issue: Literal mirror renders the を-marked direct object (テレビを) with the topic device 'As for...', which this corpus reserves for は. It falsely shows the object as a topicalized element, misrepresenting the structure the lit field must mirror.

ops.current: Quanto à televisão, coloquei em cima do suporte.
ops.fix: A televisão (を), (eu) coloquei em cima do suporte.
ops.issue: 'Quanto a...' is the corpus's mirror of は, but here it renders the direct object marked by を (テレビを), hiding the object relation and implying a topic construction that is not in the Japanese.

ops.current: As for the bath, it has heated up, see.
ops.fix: The bath (が) has heated up, see.
ops.issue: Topic device 'As for...' applied to the が-marked subject お風呂が; the corpus reserves that device for は, and the expl correctly identifies が as subject marker, so the mirror contradicts the explanation.

ops.current: Quanto ao banho, ferveu, viu.
ops.fix: O banho (が) ferveu, viu.
ops.issue: 'Quanto a...' (は device) used for the が-marked subject お風呂が; the structural mirror should reflect the subject particle, matching the expl's own analysis.

ops.current: forma い (ren'yōkei) de 泊まる, ligada ao auxiliar de passado
ops.fix: forma de ligação de 泊まる com mudança de som (促音便: 泊まり→泊まっ), ligada ao auxiliar de passado た
ops.issue: Note mislabels 泊まっ as the ren'yōkei ('forma い') of 泊まる — the ren'yōkei is 泊まり; 泊まっ is the sokuonbin (sound-changed) stem used before た. The EN version of the note repeats the same error.

ops.current: As for the way, I (humbly) show/point it out.
ops.fix: The way, (I) humbly show/point (it) out.
ops.issue: Literal mirror renders the を-marked object (道を) with the topic device 'As for...', reserved for は in this corpus; it misrepresents 道 as a topic instead of the direct object of the humble verb.

ops.current: Quanto ao caminho, faço (humildemente) o ato de ensinar/indicar.
ops.fix: O caminho (を), faço (humildemente) o ato de ensinar/indicar.
ops.issue: 'Quanto a...' (the は device) is used for the を-marked direct object 道を, implying topicalization that does not exist in the Japanese; the structural mirror should keep 道 as object.

ops.current: marked by は, which establishes the sentence's subject
ops.fix: marked by は, which establishes the sentence's theme (what it is about)
ops.full_before: The topic is 今日 (きょう, today), marked by は, which establishes the sentence's subject. The actual subject is 宿題 (しゅくだい, homework), marked by が, and the verb of existence ある closes the sentence. The adverb たくさん (a lot, in large quantity) modifies the idea of how much exists. The target here is the vocabulary 宿題.
ops.issue: Wording says は 'establishes the sentence's subject', then the next sentence says 'the actual subject is 宿題' — self-contradictory use of 'subject' for the topic. The pt version correctly uses 'assunto' (theme).

ops.current: くすりをのんだきごうするとあたまがいたくなくなった
ops.fix: くすりをのんだするとあたまがいたくなくなった
ops.issue: The full-width space in the JP was transcribed as きごう ('symbol' = 記号), inserting a phantom word into the phonetic reading: '...のんだ きごう すると...'. Reading it aloud produces a non-existent word.

ops.current: kusurionondakigousurutoatamagaitakunakunatta
ops.fix: kusurionondasurutoatamagaitakunakunatta
ops.issue: Same space-as-きごう bug leaked into romaji as 'kigou' (a phantom word). This is not the recorded punctuation/katakana known issue — it is an inserted wrong reading.

ops.current: O foco de vocabulário (alvo 1286) é o verbo 訪ねる.
ops.fix: O foco de vocabulário é o verbo 訪ねる.
ops.full_before: 日曜日に traz a partícula に marcando o ponto no tempo (no domingo). O objeto direto 祖父母 (avós) é marcado por を, e o verbo 訪ねる (visitar) aparece em 訪ねた, sua forma passada simples (informal). O foco de vocabulário (alvo 1286) é o verbo 訪ねる.
ops.issue: Internal pipeline artifact '(alvo 1286)' (a target-item ID) leaked into the learner-facing pt explanation; expl_en has no such reference, so the two versions also diverge.

ops.current: のーとをいちさつずつかった
ops.fix: のーとをいっさつずつかった
ops.issue: 一冊 is read いっさつ (issatsu, with gemination before さ), not いちさつ. The kana teaches a wrong reading of the counter word.

ops.current: いち
ops.fix: いっ
ops.issue: Token 一 in the compound 一冊 has reading いち; in context it geminates to いっ (一冊 = いっさつ), matching the pattern 一冊/一回/一杯.

ops.current: no-tooichisatsuzutsukatta
ops.fix: no-tooissatsuzutsukatta
ops.issue: Romaji carries the same wrong reading 'ichisatsu' for 一冊; correct is 'issatsu' (geminated).

ops.current: past form of 頼む (stem 頼ん + 〜だ, with i-onbin voicing)
ops.fix: en: "past form of 頼む (stem 頼ん + 〜だ, with nasal onbin 撥音便 む→ん; た voices to だ)"; pt-BR: "forma passada de 頼む (raiz 頼ん + 〜だ, com onbin nasal 撥音便 む→ん; た sonoriza para だ)"
ops.issue: Conjugation note (both en and pt-BR) says 頼んだ shows 'i-onbin voicing' (い音便). Wrong: 頼む→頼んだ is 撥音便 (hatsuonbin, nasal onbin, む→ん); い音便 is the 書いた/泳いだ type. Teaches a false conjugation classification.

ops.current: あさきごうろくじにきごうおきる
ops.fix: あさろくじにおきる
ops.issue: Both spaces in the JP were transcribed as きごう ('symbol'), inserting the phantom word twice into the phonetic reading: あさ きごう ろくじに きごう おきる.

ops.current: asakigourokujinikigouokiru
ops.fix: asarokujiniokiru
ops.issue: Same bug in romaji: 'kigou' inserted twice for the spaces. Not the recorded punctuation/katakana known issue — it is an inserted wrong reading.

ops.current: already
ops.fix: no more, (not) anymore
ops.issue: In もうない, もう + negative means '(not) anymore / no more', not 'already' (its affirmative sense). The en gloss fits the other sense; the pt gloss 'já' works because pt-BR uses 'já não'.

ops.current: That cup is made of glass.
ops.fix: This cup is made of glass.
ops.issue: この means 'this' (proximal), but the natural EN translation uses the distal 'That cup'. Demonstrative mismatch with the JP; lit_en itself correctly uses 'this'. In a course teaching ko-so-a-do this misteaches the contrast.

ops.current: this/that
ops.fix: this
ops.issue: この is glossed 'this/that'; この is proximal only — 'that' belongs to その/あの. Other sentences in the corpus gloss この correctly as 'this'.

ops.current: caro (forma て: 'mesmo que seja caro')
ops.fix: caro
ops.issue: The pt gloss claims 高い is a て-form meaning 'mesmo que seja caro' (even if expensive) — a copy-paste leftover from a 〜ても sentence. Here 高い is the plain dictionary-form predicate, exactly as the token's own note says. Teaches a false conjugation.

ops.current: As for the room, after making it clean, I put away the books.
ops.fix: Making the room clean, and after that, I put away the books.
ops.issue: 部屋を is the を-marked direct object of きれいにする, not a topic. 'As for the room' is the mirror reserved for は-topics and misrepresents the structure (there is no は in the sentence).

ops.current: Quanto ao quarto, tornando-o bonito/limpo, e a partir daí, guardei os livros.
ops.fix: Tornando o quarto limpo/bonito, e a partir daí, guardei os livros.
ops.issue: Mesma falha estrutural: 'Quanto ao quarto' apresenta o objeto marcado por を como se fosse tópico marcado por は; o espelho literal deve refletir 部屋を como objeto de きれいにする.

ops.current: むずかしいことばがありますきごうたとえばこのかんじ
ops.fix: むずかしいことばがあります たとえばこのかんじ
ops.issue: Extra syllables きごう ('symbol') injected between あります and たとえば — the whitespace token's bogus reading (tokens[5]) leaked into the transcription. The word きごう does not exist in the sentence.

ops.current: muzukashiikotobagaarimasukigoutatoebakonokanji
ops.fix: muzukashiikotobagaarimasutatoebakonokanji
ops.issue: Same leak as kana: spurious 'kigou' inserted mid-sentence; not part of the Japanese.

ops.current: He bought three apples.
ops.fix: (I) bought three apples.
ops.issue: lit_en uses subject 'He' while en uses 'I'. The JP is subjectless; default reading (and the en/pt/expl) is first person. Contradictory subject in the literal mirror confuses learners.

ops.current: forma 買っ (passado) de 買う, com sonorização antes de た
ops.fix: forma 買っ (passado) de 買う, com geminação (促音便, っ) antes de た
ops.issue: pt-BR note says 買った involves 'sonorização' (voicing) before た. False: 買う→買った is 促音便 (gemination, っ); no voicing occurs (voicing would give だ, as in 読んだ). Teaches a wrong conjugation fact; the en note ('sound change') is vague but not wrong.

ops.current: In free time, as for movies, I watch them.
ops.fix: In free time, movies (object), I watch.
ops.issue: 'as for movies' renders the を-marked direct object 映画を as a topic construction; there is no は on 映画. Contradicts the expl, which correctly calls 映画 the direct object marked by を.

ops.current: Em época que é livre, quanto a filme, assisto.
ops.fix: Em época que é livre, filme (objeto), assisto.
ops.issue: 'quanto a filme' applies the は-topic mirror device to 映画を, which is a を-marked direct object, not a topic. Misteaches particle function and contradicts the expl (objeto direto marcado por を).

ops.current: O verbo 走ります (andar/correr) está na forma polite (ます).
ops.fix: O verbo 走ります (andar/correr) está na forma polida (ます).
ops.full_before: A estrutura é tópico (車は = quanto ao carro) seguido do que ele faz. O verbo 走ります (andar/correr) está na forma polite (ます). Aqui 左側を (o lado esquerdo) usa を porque é o trajeto/espaço percorrido pelo movimento, um uso especial de を com verbos de deslocamento.
ops.issue: English word 'polite' left untranslated in the pt-BR explanation; the corpus elsewhere consistently uses 'polida/polido' (cf. same item's token note 'forma polida').

ops.current: As for every month, on the 1st, I do the cleaning.
ops.fix: Every month, on the 1st, I do the cleaning.
ops.issue: 'As for every month' fabricates a topic construction; 毎月１日 is a single time expression marked only by に (no は). The 'as for' device should be reserved for は.

ops.current: Quanto a todo mês, no dia 1, faço a limpeza.
ops.fix: Todo mês, no dia 1, faço a limpeza.
ops.issue: 'Quanto a todo mês' applies the は-topic mirror device to 毎月, which carries no は; 毎月１日 is one time expression with に. Misleads learners scanning for a topic particle.

ops.current: economy
ops.fix: economics
ops.issue: 経済 glossed as 'economy', but in 大学で経済を勉強しています it is the academic discipline, i.e. 'economics' (as the en translation itself says). Gloss fits another sense of the word, not this context.

ops.current: funciona sozinho como predicado, sем precisar de です
ops.fix: funciona sozinho como predicado, sem precisar de です
ops.full_before: Frase do tipo 'A é adjetivo'. O tópico この神社 (este santuário) é marcado por は, とても é o advérbio de intensidade ('muito'), e 古い é um い-adjetivo que funciona sozinho como predicado, sем precisar de です no registro casual. O alvo de vocabulário aqui é 神社 (santuário).
ops.issue: Encoding defect: the word 'sem' is written with Cyrillic letters е (U+0435) and м (U+043C) — 'sем' — instead of Latin characters.

ops.current: dia(do mês) (sufixo contador)
ops.fix: dia (do mês) (sufixo contador)
ops.issue: Typo: missing space before the parenthesis in 'dia(do mês)'.

ops.current: １日は (the first day) is the subject marked by は
ops.fix: １日は (the first day) is the topic marked by は
ops.full_before: Simple nominal sentence in the polite register: topic plus predicate. １日は (the first day) is the subject marked by は, and 休みです (is a day off) is the predicate, formed by the noun 休み (rest/day off) plus the polite copula です. ついたち is the special reading of 1日 (the first day of the month).
ops.issue: Calls １日は the 'subject marked by は'; は marks the topic. Inconsistent with the same sentence's opening ('topic plus predicate'), with expl_pt ('assunto'), and with the token role 'tópico'.

ops.current: このべいわとてもおいしい
ops.fix: このこめわとてもおいしい
ops.issue: 米 as a standalone noun is read こめ, not the on'yomi べい (used only in compounds like 米国). The item's own expl_en/expl_pt even state 'Here 米 is read こめ', contradicting the kana.

ops.current: konobeiwatotemooishii
ops.fix: konokomewatotemooishii
ops.issue: Romaji propagates the wrong reading 'bei' for 米; should reflect こめ (kome).

ops.current: べい
ops.fix: こめ
ops.issue: Reading of 米 in this sentence is こめ (standalone noun 'rice'); べい is the compound-only on'yomi and is wrong in context. Explanation fields correctly say こめ.

ops.current: vira o sujeito de quem se gosta, marcado por が
ops.fix: vira o sujeito do que se gosta, marcado por が
ops.full_before: A frase usa o padrão 〜のがすきです, que serve para dizer que se gosta de FAZER alguma coisa. O verbo 読む (ler) é transformado em substantivo pela partícula nominalizadora の, e essa ação inteira (本を読む = ler livros) vira o sujeito de quem se gosta, marcado por が. No fim, すきです (gostar) é um 形状詞 (adjetivo-na) que descreve a preferência. O tópico わたしは indica de quem é o gosto.
ops.issue: 'de quem se gosta' uses 'quem' (for people) although the referent is the action 本を読む; the English version says 'the subject of what is liked'. Should be 'do que se gosta'.

ops.current: com frequência, bastante (quite often, a lot)
ops.fix: com frequência, bastante
ops.issue: English text leaked into the Portuguese gloss of よく: '(quite often, a lot)'. The same word is glossed cleanly in other sentences (e.g. 'frequentemente, bastante').

ops.current: Recentemente, quanto ao trabalho, (ele) aumentou e (estou) ocupado.
ops.fix: Recentemente, o trabalho aumentou e (estou) ocupado.
ops.issue: 仕事が is a が-marked subject, but lit_pt renders it with the topic device 'quanto ao trabalho', which this corpus reserves for は; lit_en correctly has no topic phrase. Misrepresents が as topic and blurs the は/が distinction.

ops.current: どあがひらく
ops.fix: どあがあく
ops.issue: Reading ひらく clashes with the lesson: the expl teaches the jidoshi/tadoshi pair 開く⇔開ける, which is the あく/あける pair. ひらく is ambitransitive (本を開く), so the 'intransitive verb' claim only holds cleanly with あく; N4 convention for ドアが開く is あく.

ops.current: A porta abre-se.
ops.fix: A porta se abre.
ops.issue: Enclisis after an explicit subject ('A porta abre-se') is European-Portuguese wording; natural pt-BR uses proclisis with the pronominal verb.

ops.current: ひらく
ops.fix: あく

ops.fix: (null — whitespace token has no reading)

ops.current: Quanto a pergunta(s), uma (delas) existe / há.

ops.current: This table is very sturdy.

ops.issue: 机 is 'desk' (テーブル = table); lit_en and expl_en both say 'desk' while the main translation says 'table' — inconsistent and loose for a vocab-focused card.

ops.current: As for the teacher, he said that he has already come back.

ops.current: small / short
ops.fix: small / quiet (of a voice)
ops.issue: 小さい glossed 'small / short'; 'short' (stature sense) does not fit a voice. In this context it means small/quiet (of a voice), as the expl itself says ('low/quiet').

ops.current: dia(dia de chuva: 雨の日)
ops.fix: dia (dia de chuva: 雨の日)
ops.issue: Missing space before the parenthesis in the pt gloss of 日: 'dia(dia de chuva...' — typo.

ops.current: warm, lukewarm
ops.fix: warm (pleasantly hot)
ops.issue: 温かく glossed 'warm, lukewarm'; 'lukewarm' corresponds to ぬるい and carries a negative nuance — wrong for 温かい, especially when heating soup to a pleasant warmth.

ops.current: quente (agradável), ameno
ops.fix: quente (agradável), quentinho
ops.issue: Pt gloss of 温かく includes 'ameno', which in pt-BR describes mild weather/climate, not food temperature; it does not fit warming soup.

ops.current: このころすこしつかれている
ops.fix: このごろすこしつかれている

ops.current: konokorosukoshitsukareteiru
ops.fix: konogorosukoshitsukareteiru
ops.issue: Romaji inherits the wrong reading このころ; for the 'lately' sense it should be konogoro.

ops.current: nine
ops.fix: this
ops.issue: この is glossed 'nine'. この is the demonstrative 'this' (part of この頃 'these days'); 'nine' is a completely wrong word (likely corruption from ここの 九).

ops.current: nove
ops.fix: este, esta
ops.issue: この is glossed 'nove' (nine). この is the demonstrative 'este/esta'; the numeral gloss is flatly wrong and would teach a false meaning.

ops.current: ころ
ops.fix: ごろ
ops.issue: Token 頃 in この頃 'lately' must read ごろ (rendaku, このごろ), not ころ, matching the kana fix.

ops.current: O foco de vocabulário (alvo 1285) é justamente この頃.
ops.fix: O foco de vocabulário é justamente この頃.
ops.full_before: A frase abre com a expressão de tempo この頃 (ultimamente, nestes últimos tempos), seguida do advérbio 少し (um pouco). O verbo central é 疲れる (cansar-se) na forma 〜ている (疲れている), que aqui indica um estado resultante: não é a ação de cansar, mas a condição de estar cansado agora. O foco de vocabulário (alvo 1285) é justamente この頃.
ops.issue: Internal target ID '(alvo 1285)' leaked into learner-facing pt explanation; absent from expl_en. Should be removed.

ops.current: again
ops.fix: or (part of または)
ops.issue: また is glossed 'again', but here it is not the adverb また: it is part of the conjunction または 'or' — the very lesson focus per expl. The gloss makes the learner misparse the sentence.

ops.current: de novo
ops.fix: ou (parte de または)
ops.issue: また glossed 'de novo' (again), but in this sentence it is part of the conjunction または 'ou', the lesson target; the adverb gloss is wrong in context.

ops.current: My room faces south.

ops.current: Meu quarto fica para o lado sul.
ops.fix: Meu quarto fica do lado sul.
ops.issue: 'Fica para o lado sul' reads as orientation in BR Portuguese (the room faces south), but 南にあります states location; inconsistent with lit_pt 'ele existe ao sul' and the expl's location analysis.

ops.current: lugar (advérbio de lugar)
ops.fix: lugar (adjunto de lugar)
ops.issue: 南 is a noun serving as a locative complement with に, not an adverb; parallel sentences in the corpus label this 'adjunto de lugar' (cf. 部屋に in sent:gen-f357e5a73e0e), so 'advérbio de lugar' misidentifies the word class.

ops.current: にわにねこがいちひきいる
ops.fix: にわにねこがいっぴきいる
ops.issue: 一匹 undergoes obligatory sound change and is read いっぴき, never いちひき. The kana teaches a wrong pronunciation of the counter phrase.

ops.current: niwaninekogaichihikiiru
ops.fix: niwaninekogaippikiiru
ops.issue: Same counter reading error as kana: 一匹 is ippiki, not ichihiki.

ops.current: いち
ops.fix: いっ
ops.issue: In the compound 一匹 the numeral 一 is read いっ (geminated before the p-sound); the token reading いち is wrong in this context.

ops.current: ひき
ops.fix: ぴき
ops.issue: In 一匹 the counter 匹 is read ぴき (h→p after the geminate); ひき is wrong in this context.

ops.current: こんやわなんもたべないつもりです
ops.fix: こんやわなにもたべないつもりです
ops.issue: 何も is standardly read なにも; なんも is a casual colloquial contraction that clashes with the polite です register and should not be taught as the reading here.

ops.current: konyawananmotabenaitsumoridesu
ops.fix: konyawananimotabenaitsumoridesu
ops.issue: Follows the kana error: 何も should be romanized nanimo, not nanmo, in this polite sentence.

ops.current: なん

ops.current: Note that ので requires the だ form at its head (here it appears as で after the past た, forming たので).

ops.full_before: The first clause (電車が動き出した) is the cause, and ので links it to the result (座った = 'I sat down'), with the sense of 'since/because'. The grammar focus is 〜出す: the verb 動く ('to move') becomes the stem 動き and takes 出す, forming 動き出す = 'to start moving'. Note that ので requires the だ form at its head (here it appears as で after the past た, forming たので).
ops.issue: False grammar claim: says ので requires the だ form, with だ 'appearing as で after the past た'. ので attaches directly to plain verb forms (動き出した+ので); no だ is required or transformed after た; only nouns/na-adjectives insert な (なので).

ops.current: Note que ので exige a forma だ antes dele (aqui aparece como で após o passado た, formando たので).

O foco gramatical é 〜出す: o verbo 動く ('mover-se') vira radical 動き e recebe 出す, formando 動き出す = 'começar a se mover'. Note que ので exige a forma だ antes dele (aqui aparece como で após o passado た, formando たので).
ops.issue: Same false claim as expl_en: 'ので exige a forma だ antes dele'. ので attaches directly to plain verb forms (動き出した+ので); nothing appears before ので here, and nouns/na-adjectives use な (なので). Teaches a false attachment rule to beginners.

ops.full_before: 火事の時は ('at the time of a fire') is temporal/conditional, 火事 + の + 時, marked as topic by は. Core is 鳴らせ: base 鳴ら- takes the causative せ (of せる), forming 鳴らせ ('make it sound'), used as a command. Final よ reinforces the instruction. Note the parser treated 鳴ら as 鳴る + causative; in practice it equals the transitive 鳴らす ('to ring').
ops.issue: 鳴らせ is the imperative (命令形) of transitive 鳴らす plus emphatic particle よ — exactly the analysis sibling sentence 186677 gives. It is not stem + causative せ 'used as a command'; a bare causative stem cannot function as an imperative.

O núcleo é o verbo 鳴らせ: a base 鳴ら- recebe o sufixo causativo せ (de せる), formando 鳴らせ ('faça soar'), aqui usado como ordem. A frase termina com a partícula よ, que reforça a instrução. ops.fix: Leia 何か + あった + かい: あった é o passado de ある ('aconteceu/houve') e かい é partícula informal de pergunta — não é o adjetivo あったかい ('quentinho').
ops.full_before: A frase correta é 何か + あった + かい. A segmentação automática juntou あった+かい como se fosse o adjetivo あったかい ('quentinho'), mas pelo sentido ('Is anything up?') trata-se de 何か ('alguma coisa') + あった (passado de ある, 'existir/haver/acontecer') + a partícula かい. かい é a partícula de pergunta informal e amistosa. Resultado: 'Aconteceu alguma coisa?'.
ops.issue: Same pipeline-internal wording in pt ('A segmentação automática juntou...'); rewrite as a direct teaching note.

ops.current: there was, it happened (from ある); the segmentation 'あったかい'='warm' is incorrect here (read as あった + かい)

ops.issue: Token gloss contains editorial meta-commentary about the tokenizer's bad segmentation instead of a clean gloss; ideally the token should be split into あった + かい, and the gloss should just gloss.

ops.current: houve, aconteceu (de ある); a segmentação 'あったかい'='quentinho' está incorreta aqui (leia-se あった + かい)
ops.fix: houve / aconteceu (あった, passado de ある, + partícula informal de pergunta かい)

ops.current: I'm gonna shoot him.

ops.fix: I'll punish (him) / teach (him) a lesson.
ops.issue: Inaccurate literal mirror: uses 'you' while en/pt/lit_pt target 'him'; 'go and' implies a motion verb absent from the JP (やる = do-to-someone, not go); 'a good talking-to' (verbal scolding) undertranslates こらしめる (punish).

ops.fix: Vou puni-lo / dar-lhe um corretivo.

ops.current: How long (a time) was (it)?
ops.fix: How long (a time) were (you) (there)?
ops.issue: '(it)' implies an inanimate subject, but いた is the animate verb いる ('you/he stayed'); the item's own expl and en ('How long did you stay?') confirm an animate subject. lit_pt has no such '(it)'.

ops.current: にっぽんえいけたらいいのに。
ops.fix: にほんえいけたらいいのに。

ops.current: That's a silly (adjectival) question, it's just that.
ops.fix: A silly (adjectival) question exists, it's just that.
ops.issue: 質問がある is existential ('a silly question exists'), but the literal renders it as a copula ('That's a silly question'), misrepresenting the structure the literal field must mirror. lit_pt correctly uses 'existe'.

ops.current: We take the verb 書く/かく (here かく in the sense of 'to snore', いびきをかく = 'to snore')
ops.fix: We take the verb かく (掻く, usually written in kana — not 書く 'to write'; いびきをかく = 'to snore')
ops.full_before: This sentence uses the target 〜たことがある, the pattern that expresses past experience ('I have done it at some time'). We take the verb 書く/かく (here かく in the sense of 'to snore', いびきをかく = 'to snore'), put it in the past form かいた and add ことがある, literally 'there is the thing of having done'. The が marks こと (the experience) as the subject of ある ('to exist/there is'). The rising intonation of the ？ turns it all into an informal question.
ops.issue: The verb of いびきをかく is misidentified as 書く ('to write'). The idiom uses かく = 掻く (normally written in kana), not 書く. This teaches a false verb/kanji identity to learners.

ops.current: Tomamos o verbo 書く/かく (aqui かく no sentido de 'roncar', いびきをかく = 'roncar')
ops.fix: Tomamos o verbo かく (掻く, normalmente em kana — não 書く 'escrever'; いびきをかく = 'roncar')
ops.full_before: Esta frase usa o alvo 〜たことがある, o padrão que expressa experiência passada ('já fiz alguma vez'). Tomamos o verbo 書く/かく (aqui かく no sentido de 'roncar', いびきをかく = 'roncar'), colocamos na forma passada かいた e adicionamos ことがある, literalmente 'há a coisa de ter feito'. O が marca こと (a experiência) como sujeito de ある ('existir/haver'). A entonação ascendente do ？ transforma tudo em pergunta informal.
ops.issue: Same false fact as expl_en: the verb of いびきをかく is identified as 書く ('escrever'); it is actually かく = 掻く (normalmente em kana), unrelated to 書く.

ops.current: A partícula final と liga essa oração ao verbo 思う ('achar').
ops.fix: A partícula と liga essa oração ao verbo 思う ('achar').
ops.full_before: A frase termina em 〜と思う (alvo), que marca a opinião/suposição de quem fala: a parte antes do と é o conteúdo do pensamento. Aqui o conteúdo é 何をしてた ('o que eu estava fazendo'), em que してた é a forma coloquial contraída de していた (している no passado, indicando ação em andamento). A partícula final と liga essa oração ao verbo 思う ('achar'). Como a frase é uma pergunta (？), o sentido é 'o que você acha que eu estava fazendo?'.
ops.issue: と here is the quotative particle, not a 'partícula final' (sentence-final particle class like よ/ね); the label teaches a wrong particle category. expl_en correctly says just 'The particle と'.

ops.current: As for foreign countries, they're interesting, huh.

ops.current: Someday I'll run like the wind.
ops.fix: Someday I'll run like the wind again.

ops.current: ('e olha que era nova'. Aqui の é nominalizador e に completa のに.)
ops.fix: ('e olha que era nova'). Aqui の é nominalizador e に completa のに.
ops.full_before: Exclamação emotiva, deixada pela metade. 私の白いズボンが é 'minha calça branca' (の = posse, 白い = adjetivo branco, が marca o sujeito) e a frase é interrompida no が, com o verbo subentendido pelo contexto (sujou/estragou). Depois, 新しいのに usa 〜のに ('apesar de / logo agora que'): 新しい (nova) + のに expressa frustração ('e olha que era nova'. Aqui の é nominalizador e に completa のに.)
ops.issue: Misplaced closing parenthesis: it wrongly wraps the following sentence inside the gloss parenthetical (compare expl_en, where the parenthesis closes right after 'and they were even new').

ops.current: Note that there is no だ before かい because 同じ functions as the predicate.
ops.fix: Note that there is no だ before かい: the plain copula だ is normally dropped before か/かい.
ops.full_before: The sentence has as its topic それら ('those', marked by は), then みんな ('all') and the na-adjective 同じ ('the same'). The grammatical target is the final particle かい, which here appears as か + い together (かい): it is an informal and gentle way of asking a yes/no question, typical of masculine speech or of speaking with someone close. Note that there is no だ before かい because 同じ functions as the predicate.
ops.issue: Wrong reason for the missing copula: だ is absent because plain だ is regularly dropped before か/かい after any noun/na-adjective, not because 同じ 'functions as the predicate' (as a plain statement it would be 同じだ).

ops.current: Repare que não há だ antes de かい porque 同じ funciona como o predicado.
ops.fix: Repare que não há だ antes de かい: a cópula だ normalmente é omitida antes de か/かい.
ops.full_before: A frase tem como tópico それら ("aqueles", marcado por は), depois みんな ("todos") e o adjetivo-な 同じ ("igual"). O alvo gramatical é a partícula final かい, que aqui aparece como か + い juntas (かい): é uma forma informal e suave de fazer uma pergunta de sim/não, típica da fala masculina ou de quem fala com alguém próximo. Repare que não há だ antes de かい porque 同じ funciona como o predicado.
ops.issue: Same wrong grammar reason as expl_en: the absence of だ is due to the general rule that だ is omitted before か/かい, not to 同じ 'funcionar como predicado' (a afirmação simples seria 同じだ).

ops.current: なかった (past of ない, "to not exist") + たら = なかったら
ops.fix: なかっ- (past stem of ない) + たら = なかったら ("if there isn't / without")
ops.full_before: The target is the conditional 〜たら, here applied to a negative adjective: なかった (past of ない, "to not exist") + たら = なかったら ("if there isn't / without"). The main clause is 生きていけない, a combination of 生きる + ていく (living "going forward") in the negative potential いけない ("I can't live"). よ at the end asserts the idea with emphasis to the listener.
ops.issue: Morphology formula double-counts た: 'なかった + たら' would yield *なかったたら. Correct segmentation is なかっ + たら (matching the token split なかっ|たら) or なかった + ら.

ops.current: なかった (passado de ない, "não existir") + たら = なかったら
ops.fix: なかっ- (radical do passado de ない) + たら = なかったら ("se não houver / sem")
ops.full_before: O alvo é o condicional 〜たら, aqui aplicado a um adjetivo negativo: なかった (passado de ない, "não existir") + たら = なかったら ("se não houver / sem"). A oração principal é 生きていけない, junção de 生きる + ていく (viver "indo adiante") na forma potencial negativa いけない ("não consigo viver"). よ no fim afirma a ideia com ênfase ao ouvinte.
ops.issue: Same formula error as expl_en: 'なかった + たら' duplica o た e produziria *なかったたら; a segmentação correta é なかっ + たら (como nos tokens) ou なかった + ら.

ops.current: O verbo está em forma progressiva しているている: している = 'estão arruinando'

Dentro do conteúdo: 試験が ('as provas', sujeito) e 教育を ('a educação', objeto) com o padrão 〜を駄目にする ('tornar X inútil / arruinar X'). O verbo está em forma progressiva しているている: している = 'estão arruinando', uma ação em andamento.
ops.issue: Garbled duplication 'しているている' (expl_en correctly has just している); the sentence also reads better as 'na forma progressiva'.

ops.current: ません + ん (de ぬ) reforça a negação na fala formal/escrita.
